Lessons.Title: Differences of Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will use a number line to reason about subtraction of fractions with the same denominator.
Key idea: Subtracting like-denominator fractions can be modeled as a leftward jump or distance on a number line.
How to reason: Subtract equal-sized numerator parts and retain the denominator, with regrouping where needed.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up: True or False: Sums of Tenths (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1: Jump to Subtract (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{11}{6}\), Number line. 13 evenly spaced tick marks. First tick mark, 0. Seventh, 1. Thirteenth, 2. Arrow from point at twelfth tick mark, labeled eleven sixths to fifth tick mark., Number line. 13 evenly spaced tick marks. First tick mark, 0. Seventh, 1. Thirteenth, 2. Arrow from point at twelfth tick mark, labeled eleven sixths to ninth tick mark., Number line. 13 evenly spaced tick marks. First tick mark, 0. Seventh, 1. Thirteenth, 2. Arrow from point at twelfth tick mark, labeled eleven sixths to seventh tick mark.. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2: What’s the Difference? (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{13}{8} - \frac{2}{8}\), \(\frac{13}{8} - \frac{6}{8}\), \(\frac{13}{8} - 1\), \(1\frac{5}{8} - \frac{7}{8}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 3: Make a Jump, Subtraction Edition [OPTIONAL] (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to the original contexts or representations. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
